title: Integrity cost engineering — precompute-extract + prompt-slim the mechanical checks; defer Haiku split. (DIRECTIVE-20260620-002)
why_human_needed: Phase-1 path selection (precompute vs prompt-slim vs Haiku split) is an operator call; Haiku-eligibility claims require a smoke-test the operator should sanction; coverage-preservation on a structure-integrity agent is correctness-sensitive.
do_not_auto_close_reason: propose-only / requires_human_judgment; closure is operator-driven after a phase is chosen and shipped.
summary: Integrity costs a stable ~$4.24/run ($21/wk, ~$1.1K/yr). The cost is genuine and worth engineering. The cost is dominated by cache_read (55%, the ~855-line prompt + reference prefix re-read across ~70 turns) and cache_write_1h (29%, the big prompt cached cold each daily run), NOT by file-walking per se — large-file scans run inside bash node -e blocks that print SHORT summaries, so most bytes never enter LLM context (same mechanism PROP-104 found for decider). The highest-ROI, lowest-risk levers are therefore (A) precompute-extract the mechanical checks (1/1b/4/5/6) into one deterministic compute-integrity-mechanical.js the LLM consumes as a single small JSON — mirrors PROP-020/021 — which cuts turns + output + tool_result accumulation; and (B) prompt-slim by moving rare-path forensic prose (the 7h PROP-078 prologue, 7e digest mechanics, schema-correction notes) to a reference file. A Haiku model-split is real but only ~3x cheaper (NOT 10x — see correction) and carries coverage/handoff risk, so it is deferred to Phase 2 conditional on (A)+(B) being insufficient and on smoke-test evidence.

the_correction_up_front.wall_clock_premise_is_a_skewed_mean_arti: The directive's headline '3931s = ~65 min per run' is a MEAN dominated by a single outlier. Per monitor/integrity/cost-history.jsonl (6 runs, 2026-06-15..06-20): transcript_duration_sec = [447, 563, 576, 585, 605, 17462]. Five of six runs are 447-605s (~7.5-10 min). The sixth (2026-06-19, 17462s = 4.85 h) drags the mean to 3373s. MEDIAN is 580s (9.7 min); mean-excluding-outlier is 555s (9.3 min). The typical integrity run is ~9 minutes, not 65. So 'it takes 65 minutes for a structure check' is NOT the real situation; the 06-19 run is a stall to investigate separately, not evidence of systemic 65-min runtime.
the_correction_up_front.cost_premise_IS_correct: The COST concern is real and stable: total_usd = $3.64-$4.74 across ALL six runs including the slow one (mean $4.242, matching the directive). Cost is decoupled from wall-clock — the 4.85h run cost $4.74, only ~12% above the median run. So cost engineering is justified on its own terms; wall-clock is a separate, smaller, outlier-driven concern.
the_correction_up_front.composition_confirms_directive: Cost split (mean of 6): cache_read 55.1% ($2.34), cache_write_1h 29.2% ($1.24), output 15.7% ($0.67), input ~0%. This matches the directive's '29% write, 56% read, 15% out' table line. The driver is the ~70-turn conversation prefix re-read (cache_read) on top of a large cold-cached prompt (cache_write), exactly the PROP-104 the_correction pattern.
the_correction_up_front.haiku_savings_overstated_in_directive: The directive's Q3 says 'Haiku at 0.1x the read cost = ~10x savings.' That conflates Haiku's ABSOLUTE cache_read rate ($0.10/MTok) with the MULTIPLE vs Sonnet. Per the compute-run-cost.js PRICING table: Sonnet-4-6 cache_read $0.30, Haiku-4-5 cache_read $0.10 -> 3x cheaper, not 10x. Haiku is uniformly ~3x cheaper across in/out/cache_read/cache_write_1h. A clean Haiku swap (same token volume, IF quality holds) would be ~$1.4/run vs $4.24 = ~3x / 67% — better than the directive's 40% split estimate, but only if Haiku does the semantic checks without quality loss, which is unproven.
the_correction_up_front.file_size_nit: Directive says integrity 'walks docs/index.html (4.5MB HTML)'. Actual size on git HEAD is 1.75MB (docs/index.html), sections.json 759KB, wins.json 588KB. Minor, but the precompute-savings estimate should use real sizes.

Q1_per_check_token_wallclock_attribution.status: PARTIAL — aggregate measured, per-check attribution requires Phase 0 instrumentation
Q1_per_check_token_wallclock_attribution.what_is_measured_now: Aggregate per-run from cost-history.jsonl (N=6): mean $4.242/run, ~70 assistant turns, cache_read 55% / cache_write 29% / output 16%, median 9.7 min wall-clock.
Q1_per_check_token_wallclock_attribution.what_is_NOT_measured_yet: Per-check token + wall-clock breakdown. cost-history.jsonl is whole-run only. We cannot yet say which of Checks 1-9 dominates.
Q1_per_check_token_wallclock_attribution.phase_0_instrumentation: Mirror PROP-104's STEP_MARKER pattern: emit a no-op stderr breadcrumb `STEP_MARKER <check-id> <epoch>` at the start of each check's bash block in structure-integrity.md (Checks 1,1b,2,3,4,5,5b,5c,5d,6,7,7a.5,7a.6,7b-7i,8,9). Then ship a compute-integrity-step-cost.js (clone of compute-decider-step-cost.js) that buckets the live transcript's tokens by check window. Capture 3-5 runs. ~30 bytes/marker, zero behavioral impact. EXIT criterion: >=3 instrumented runs before any Phase-1 model/split decision.
Q1_per_check_token_wallclock_attribution.predicted_ranking_to_be_tested: From the prompt structure, the likely top token-consumers are Check 5 (per-WIN detail loop over ~70 WINs), Check 4 (data-prose rebuild), Check 1/1b (full-HTML anchor + href walks), and Check 5b (dome-site fetch). Likely top WALL-CLOCK consumer is Check 3 (External Link Validation, ~30 HTTP calls x up to 15s timeout) and Check 5b (network fetch of the dome wins page). The two rankings differ: token cost tracks turns+prefix; wall-clock tracks network I/O. The 06-19 outlier is almost certainly a Check-3/Check-5b network stall.

Q2_mechanical_vs_semantic_classification.legend: MECHANICAL = file-exists/count-matches/anchor-resolves/hash-matches/HTTP-status — scriptable or Haiku-able. SEMANTIC = cross-reference judgment — Sonnet. MIXED = mechanical scan + semantic interpretation — splittable.

checks.1_internal_anchor_integrity: MECHANICAL — id/href resolution, sectionNav chain continuity, TOC targets. Pure graph check.
checks.1b_relative_href_resolution: MECHANICAL — already a self-contained node script inline in the prompt; trivially extractable.
checks.2_tab_structure: MECHANICAL — unique IDs, nav references, non-empty tabs, heading hierarchy.
checks.3_external_link_validation: MECHANICAL — HTTP status classification (broken/redirect/timeout/ok). Network-bound but no judgment.
checks.4_data_prose_consistency: MECHANICAL — recompute counts from wins.json, compare to HTML. Deterministic.
checks.5_win_detail_consistency: MECHANICAL — per-WIN anchor existence, row existence, verdict-color match, group consistency, asterisk marker. Deterministic loop.
checks.5b_win_number_alignment_with_dome: MIXED — fetch+parse is mechanical; 'title/claim drift' and 'cross-reference alias' judgments are SEMANTIC (does the dome's new title still match our claim?).
checks.5c_progressive_disclosure: MOSTLY MECHANICAL — presence of <details>/<summary>/ps-tldr/ks-tldr and non-empty TLDR text. The 'is this TLDR meaningful' nuance is light-semantic but the spec is structural.
checks.5d_hardcoded_theme_colors: MECHANICAL — regex scan of sections.json inline styles (script already in prompt).
checks.6_discoverability: MECHANICAL — file existence, XML/JSON validity, meta-tag presence, count cross-checks.
checks.7_expansion_tracker_continuity: MECHANICAL — ID continuity/gaps/next_id/disjointness over live+archive (script already in prompt).
checks.7a6_fuse_vs_git_staleness: MECHANICAL — hash comparison FUSE vs git.
checks.7c_section_new_priority_queue_coupling: MIXED — mechanical coupling scan + light interpretation.
checks.7e_curmudgeon_digest_coverage: MIXED — coverage counting is mechanical; 'is this a real gap' is light-semantic.
checks.7g_drift_audit: MECHANICAL — already fully a script (compute-drift-audit.js); integrity just gates+reports.
checks.7i_curmudgeon_dispatcher_state: MECHANICAL — already fully a script (compute-curmudgeon-dispatcher-state.js); integrity just gates+reports.
checks.7h_mech_a_bypass_false_closure: MIXED — the scan is mechanical (field-match over closed-issues.json); the 're-verify target file against closure_reason' on a flagged CRITICAL is SEMANTIC.
checks.8_project_docs: MIXED — schedule-table/file-map/path checks mechanical; 'hardcoded count that should be a query' detection is light-semantic.
checks.9_build_reproducibility: MECHANICAL — node build.js html + diff vs docs/index.html.

Q2_mechanical_vs_semantic_classification.tally: ~17 MECHANICAL, ~5 MIXED, ~0 purely-SEMANTIC. The integrity charter is overwhelmingly mechanical — which is exactly why precompute-extraction (A) is the natural fit and why a full Sonnet pass over all of it is the waste.

Q3_haiku_eligibility.status: DEFERRED to Phase 0 smoke-test — no Haiku-as-integrity comparison run yet; per the directive's constraint, Haiku-eligibility claims must be smoke-test-backed, not asserted.
Q3_haiku_eligibility.reasoning: Given Q2, ~17/22 checks are MECHANICAL and would plausibly produce identical findings on Haiku (they ARE mechanical — Haiku makes fewer judgment errors on mechanical work because there is no judgment). The 5 MIXED checks (5b, 7c, 7e, 7h, 8) contain the semantic residue that wants Sonnet.
Q3_haiku_eligibility.smoke_test_design: Re-run Haiku-as-integrity against 2-3 historical days where the Sonnet integrity report had findings (e.g. 2026-06-19 PRED-073 build-drift CRITICAL; the 2026-06-18 relative-href 404). Compare finding-for-finding. If Haiku catches the same mechanical findings, that is the evidence. Cost note: Haiku is ~3x cheaper per token (not 10x — see correction), so the swap saves ~67% on whatever volume moves to Haiku.
Q3_haiku_eligibility.caveat: Even if Haiku passes the smoke-test, the split's value depends on whether (A) precompute-extraction already collapsed the token volume — if (A) drops the LLM portion to a thin report-writer, a model swap saves little in absolute dollars. Sequence (A)+(B) FIRST, then re-measure before committing to a split.

Q4_precompute_extraction_candidates.pattern: PROP-020 (drift-audit) and PROP-021 (curmudgeon-dispatcher-state) both already do this for integrity-adjacent work: a deterministic Node script writes a small JSON, the LLM consumes a summary in one read. Extend to integrity's own mechanical checks.
Q4_precompute_extraction_candidates.proposed_artifact: monitor/scripts/compute-integrity-mechanical.js -> monitor/integrity/integrity-mechanical-<RUN_ID>.json. One script runs Checks 1,1b,2,4,5,5c,5d,6,7,7a.5,7f and emits a structured {check, status, findings[]} blob. The LLM reads ONE JSON instead of writing ~11 inline bash node -e blocks across ~11+ turns.

candidates_with_estimate.savings: Removes a multi-turn HTML walk; LLM reads a {broken:[...]} list. Est. 3-5 turns -> 1 read.
Removes the recompute+compare logic from context; LLM reads {expected,actual,mismatches}. ~2 turns -> 0 (folded into the one read).
Biggest single win — the per-WIN loop is the likely #1 token-consumer (Q1). Script emits {win_id, anchor_ok, row_ok, color_ok, group_ok}[]. ~5-8 turns -> 1 read.
All already scripted inline; consolidate into the same artifact. ~4-6 turns -> folded in.

Q4_precompute_extraction_candidates.net_effect: Turn count is the cache_read multiplier. Collapsing ~11 mechanical bash-block turns into 1 artifact-read could cut assistant_msgs from ~70 toward ~30-40, with cache_read scaling roughly with turns. Conservative estimate: 25-40% total-cost reduction from precompute alone, model-independent. This is the single highest-ROI/lowest-risk lever and needs NO model change.
Q4_precompute_extraction_candidates.risk: LOW — deterministic script, LLM only reports. Same risk profile as the already-shipped PROP-020/021 scripts. Phase 0 ships it in SHADOW (script runs, integrity still does its own checks) so we can diff script-findings vs LLM-findings before cutting over.

Q5_two_agent_split_analysis.design: Mirror PROP-038 (curmudgeon discovery+verify). integrity-mechanical (Haiku/script, computes the Q4 artifact + flags every-issue-no-judgment) -> integrity-semantic (Sonnet, reads artifact summaries + applies judgment on the 5 MIXED checks + writes the final single report).
Q5_two_agent_split_analysis.cost_math: Directive's estimate ~$0.50 Haiku + ~$2 Sonnet = $2.50/run vs $4.24 = ~40%. BUT: corrected — most of integrity is mechanical, so if the Haiku/script pass does the bulk and Sonnet only adjudicates 5 MIXED checks + writes the report, the Sonnet portion could be much smaller than $2. Plausible $0.5 + $1 = $1.5/run (~65%). The uncertainty is large; Phase 0 per-check attribution (Q1) is required to bound it.
Q5_two_agent_split_analysis.risk: MEDIUM — adds a handoff + a second scheduled task. Q8 single-voice contract must be preserved. PROP-038 proved the pattern works, but integrity is correctness-sensitive (it is the pipeline's own smoke-detector).
Q5_two_agent_split_analysis.recommendation: DEFER. Do (A) precompute + (B) prompt-slim first. A split only pays if, after (A)+(B), the residual Sonnet cost is still high AND the smoke-test (Q3) clears Haiku. Re-evaluate with Phase-0 data.

Q6_external_link_cadence.finding: Check 3 makes ~30 HTTP calls/run to data-source domains (NOAA/NASA/ESA/USGS/INTERMAGNET/GitHub/tools). At up to 15s timeout each, this is the most plausible wall-clock contributor and the likely cause of the 2026-06-19 4.85h stall (a hung/retrying fetch). Token cost of Check 3 is small; its cost is wall-clock.
Q6_external_link_cadence.proposal: Move Check 3 to a 7-DAY cadence (gate on monitor/integrity/external-link-status.json generated_at > 168h), OR trigger only when a data-source URL in sections.json changes (hash the extracted URL set). Data-source pages do not vanish randomly — ESA's 2026-06-19 permanent-redirect is a once-in-many-months event; weekly latency is acceptable. Add a hard per-fetch timeout + total Check-3 budget (e.g. 90s wall) with a fail-soft 'skipped, stale' note so a single hung host can never produce a 4.85h run again.
Q6_external_link_cadence.risk: LOW — cron/gate only, no coverage loss (links still checked, just weekly). Independently removes the wall-clock outlier risk. RECOMMENDED as an immediate, standalone win even if (A)/(B) wait.

Q7_compare_to_curmudgeon_verify.data: curmudgeon-verify (sibling Sonnet mechanical-verify) cost-history: bimodal — no-op runs ~$0.90-1.03 at 54-92s (8-12 turns); active runs ~$2.5-3.9 at 207-526s (34-65 turns). Integrity is $4.24 at ~70 turns flat (no no-op mode — it always does the full 22-check sweep daily).
Q7_compare_to_curmudgeon_verify.insight: The 8x wall-clock multiplier vs verify's no-op runs is mostly that integrity has no early-exit: it runs all ~22 checks every day whether or not anything changed. verify short-circuits when there is nothing to verify. Integrity could adopt a similar gate for the network-bound + drift checks (Check 3 weekly per Q6; 7g/7i already gated at 72h/6h). The fixed per-check overhead (turn = re-read prefix) is the structural floor that precompute (A) + prompt-slim (B) attack.
Q7_compare_to_curmudgeon_verify.takeaway: Integrity's cost is ~structural, not anomalous — it just has not had the gating + precompute treatment verify-class agents got. There is real, safe headroom.

Q8_single_voice_preservation.contract: Downstream consumers (decider Priority 2b, tinker Mode 1) read ONE report-*.json + ONE latest-integrity-summary.txt at fixed paths. Any change must keep these exact outputs at the same paths.
Q8_single_voice_preservation.preserved_by_design: (A) precompute is invisible to consumers — integrity still writes the same single report, it just builds it from an artifact instead of inline scans. (B) prompt-slim is invisible. (C) cadence change is invisible (report still lists Check 3 status: 'fresh'/'stale-skipped'). Only (D) the two-agent split changes the topology: integrity-mechanical would feed integrity-semantic which writes the final report — externally identical.
Q8_single_voice_preservation.split_edge_case: If integrity-semantic crashes before writing the final report, mechanical findings are lost UNLESS the script also persists them. Mitigation: compute-integrity-mechanical.js must write its JSON to disk (monitor/integrity/integrity-mechanical-*.json) BEFORE the semantic pass, so a semantic crash leaves a recoverable mechanical artifact + an integrity report can be reconstructed. This is another reason to ship (A) the artifact first — it makes a future split safe by construction.

Ship compute-integrity-step-cost.js (clone of compute-decider-step-cost.js) for per-check attribution. Capture >=3 runs.

Run the Q3 Haiku smoke-test against 2-3 historical finding-bearing days; record finding-for-finding agreement.
Investigate the 2026-06-19 17462s outlier transcript (confirm Check 3 / Check 5b network stall hypothesis).
phase_1_pick_ONE_or_mix_on_evidence: 1A PRECOMPUTE (recommended first): cut integrity over to consuming the mechanical artifact; remove the inline bash blocks for Checks 1/1b/4/5/5c/5d/6/7/7a.5/7f. Est. 25-40% cost cut, model-independent, LOW risk.

1B PROMPT-SLIM: move rare-path forensic prose (7h PROP-078 prologue, 7e digest mechanics, schema-correction history) to monitor/prompts/reference/integrity-deep-notes.md, conditionally referenced. Cuts cache_write+cache_read floor, LOW risk.
1C EXTERNAL-LINK CADENCE (independent immediate win): Check 3 weekly + per-fetch/total timeout budget. Removes wall-clock outlier risk, LOW risk.
1D HAIKU SPLIT (only if 1A+1B insufficient AND smoke-test clears): mirror PROP-038. MEDIUM risk; preserve single-voice per Q8.
phased_rollout.recommended_sequence: 1C now (cheap, fixes the outlier) -> 1A -> 1B -> re-measure -> decide on 1D. Do NOT lead with the Haiku split.

the_other_side_arguments: AGAINST optimizing at all: $21/wk is a small line item and integrity is the pipeline's smoke-detector — correctness >> cost. Counter: 1A/1B/1C are coverage-preserving and LOW risk; they also remove the 4.85h-stall failure mode (operator-latency + a hung run blocking the 02-slot). The ROI is modest but the risk is near-zero, so it clears the bar.

AGAINST the precompute: it duplicates check logic into a script that can drift from the prompt's intent. Counter: that is exactly what PROP-020/021 already accepted and it has held; shadow-diff for >=3 runs before cutover catches drift.

AGAINST trusting the '9-minute median': N=6 is small and the 06-19 stall could recur. Counter: agreed — which is why 1C (timeout budget) is recommended regardless; it bounds the worst case rather than assuming it away.

FOR the directive's instinct even though its 65-min framing is a skewed mean: the COST is real and stable, and integrity genuinely never got the gating/precompute treatment its siblings did. The directive points at a real inefficiency; only its wall-clock magnitude is mis-stated.

confidence_and_next_measurement.what_N6_supports: Cost magnitude ($4.24/run +/- ~$0.4), composition (cache_read 55% / write 29% / out 16%), and that wall-clock is bimodal (9-min normal vs one 4.85h stall). These are solid at N=6.
confidence_and_next_measurement.what_needs_more_data: Per-check token/wall-clock attribution (need STEP_MARKER, >=3 runs). Haiku finding-parity (need smoke-test). Exact precompute savings (need shadow-diff turn-count delta). State per-check claims as hypotheses until Phase 0 lands.
confidence_and_next_measurement.bounded_claim: Precompute (1A) cost reduction is estimated 25-40% with wide error bars at N=6/no-attribution; tighter bounds need the Phase 0 per-check data.

constraints_honored: ALL 22 checks preserved — every lever is script-extraction, gating, prompt-relocation, or model-routing. Zero checks removed.

Daily 02:00Z cadence unchanged for the agent; only Check 3's INTERNAL scan cadence proposed weekly (decider's 02-slot still gets a daily report).
Haiku-eligibility left as a smoke-test (Q3), not asserted.
